newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends up after Brazil USDA attache data.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends up after Brazil USDA attache data.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices ended broadly higher on Tuesday, bolstered by speculative buying amid a bullish USDA attache report for the 1997/98 Brazil crop, traders said.

The attache report, dated May 9, put Brazil's 1997/98 harvest at 24 million 60-kg bags, down sharply from the USDA's official Brazil estimate of 28 million bags published in its 1997/98 world coffee production report in June.

"Four million bags is a big difference," said Hencorp Becstone president Victor Henriquez. "Those four million bags could represent the difference between in a price for coffee of 150 or 250 (cents per lb basis September)."

The release of the attache report also coincided with a revised 1997/98 estimate by Brazilian trade house Tristao which raised its forecast for the crop by 8.94 percent to 25.6 million bags from an April forecast of 23.5 million bags. "It's very confusing," said one trader. "No one's sure what the crop will be."

Benchmark September arabicas rose to a session high of 173.00 cents before a late bout of local long liquidation trimmed gains. By the close, September stood at 171.65 cents, up 5.95 cents a lb on the day and well off the intraday low of 165.00 cents.
Spot July ended 6.25 cents higher, at 191.50 cents, while the outer months closed up 2.25 to 3.75 cents.
After a slight dip at the outset, New York coffee prices climbed as a long-term weather forecast predicting potentially cooler temperatures in top-grower Brazil sparked speculative interest.

But U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said in an update on Tuesday that the warm ridge of high pressure recently dominating Brazil's coffee belt is expected to remain in the region for the next seven days.

Hencorp Becstone's Henriquez also said the failure of much of the coffee recently put up for exchange certification to pass CSCE approval bolstered both sentiment and the nearby July/September switch.
The July/September switch widened to 19.85 cents compared with 19.50 cents at the close on Monday, while September/December stretched to 16.30 cents from 13.85 cents.

After Tuesday's close, CSCE reported stocks rose by 2,893 60-kg bags as of July 7, to 55,369 bags. The exchange also reported that 8,152 bags were graded, but less than half -- 3,199 bags -- had passed.
An additional 34,159 bags were pending exchange approval, CSCE said.

In other news, the worldwide director of Nestle AG said he expects continued volatility in world coffee markets and cautioned that price hikes are hurting consumption -- especially in the United States and central Europe.

"Some sources presently estimate that North American consumption volume might drop by as much as 10 percent in 1997 compared to 1996," Mario Conti, director general of Nestle, told a meeting in this northwest industrial center marking the 70th anniversary of Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation.

Technically, traders said September's finish near the day's highs improved the market's recent dreary chart outlook.They said the active contract faced near-term resistance at 174.00-175.00 cents, followed by 181.00 and 184.50.
On the downside, today's low of 165.00 should supply good support, they said, with roaster interest noted in the low 160s.
Turnover was fairly light, at an estimated 5,329 lots.
